lines.text: Would the Earth move? If all of us jumped, at once.
lines.phonemes: wʊd ðɪ ˈɜːθ mˈuːv? ɪf ˈɔːl ʌv ˌʌs dʒˈʌmpt, ɐtwˈʌns.

lines.text: When you jump, you push the ground away, and the ground is the whole planet. So gather everyone into one crowd, all eight billion, and jump together.
lines.phonemes: wˌɛn juː dʒˈʌmp, juː pˈʊʃ ðə ɡɹˈaʊnd ɐwˈeɪ, ænd ðə ɡɹˈaʊnd ɪz ðə hˈoʊl plˈænɪt. sˌoʊ ɡˈæðɚɹ ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn ˌɪntʊ wˈʌn kɹˈaʊd, ˈɔːl ˈeɪt bˈɪliən, ænd dʒˈʌmp təɡˈɛðɚ.

lines.text: For about half a second we're all in the air, and the planet, pushed the other way, drops away beneath our feet.
lines.phonemes: fɔːɹ ɐbˌaʊt hˈæf ɐ sˈɛkənd wɪɹ ˈɔːl ɪnðɪ ˈɛɹ, ænd ðə plˈænɪt, pˈʊʃt ðɪ ˈʌðɚ wˈeɪ, dɹˈɑːps ɐwˈeɪ bᵻnˌiːθ ˌaʊɚ fˈiːt.

lines.text: It sounds like it should knock the planet off course. But the push is shared out by weight, and the Earth outweighs all of us ten trillion times over.
lines.phonemes: ɪt sˈaʊndz lˈaɪk ɪt ʃˌʊd nˈɑːk ðə plˈænɪt ˈɔf kˈɔːɹs. bˌʌt ðə pˈʊʃ ɪz ʃˈɛɹd ˈaʊt baɪ wˈeɪt, ænd ðɪ ˈɜːθ aʊtwˈeɪz ˈɔːl ʌv ˌʌs tˈɛn tɹˈɪliən tˈaɪmz ˈoʊvɚ.

lines.text: So the whole planet moves a distance three thousand times smaller than a single atom. And when we land, it settles right back where it was.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ ðə hˈoʊl plˈænɪt mˈuːvz ɐ dˈɪstəns θɹˈiː θˈaʊzənd tˈaɪmz smˈɔːlɚ ðˌænə sˈɪŋɡəl ˈæɾəm. ænd wɛn wiː lˈænd, ɪt sˈɛɾəlz ɹˈaɪt bˈæk wˌɛɹ ɪt wˈʌz.

lines.text: Jump higher, or count us lighter, and it stays thousands of times smaller than an atom.
lines.phonemes: dʒˈʌmp hˈaɪɚ, ɔːɹ kˈaʊnt ˌʌs lˈaɪɾɚ, ænd ɪt stˈeɪz θˈaʊzəndz ʌv tˈaɪmz smˈɔːlɚ ðˌænən ˈæɾəm.

lines.text: So yes, the Earth moves when we jump. It just never notices.
lines.phonemes: sˌoʊ jˈɛs, ðɪ ˈɜːθ mˈuːvz wɛn wiː dʒˈʌmp. ɪt dʒˈʌst nˈɛvɚ nˈoʊɾɪsᵻz.

lines.text: Next envelope: what if a whole day's rain fell in one second?
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: wˌʌt ɪf ɐ hˈoʊl dˈeɪz ɹˈeɪn fˈɛl ɪn wˈʌn sˈɛkənd?
